//:
§3.3 fp_viewer, checked in this order. (0) The SDP has no bare CR (a  not immediately followed by 
) anywhere, else why line_end. (1) Lines split on 
 or 
; the candidates are every line that, after leading spaces and tabs, case-insensitively starts with "a=fingerprint:" (session level and every m=); none -> why none. (2) Each candidate, top to bottom: starts exactly with lowercase "a=fingerprint:" at its first character (no other case, no leading whitespace; str0m would not use such a line, so it is refused, not skipped) else name; then exactly `a=fingerprint:sha-256 <hex>`: `<alg> <value>` split at the first space with a non-empty algorithm else form (`a=fingerprint: sha-256 ...` has an empty algorithm), algorithm exactly lowercase sha-256 else alg, value 32 bytes as 2-digit hex pairs joined by ':' (hex any case) and nothing else (no trailing whitespace, no NUL) else form; every value equal to the first else mismatch. (3) >= 1 line, all values equal -> fp_viewer. Any failure is proof_invalid:fp_bad; why = the first failing check, in this order: line_end -> none -> per line top to bottom: name -> form (no split, or empty algorithm) -> alg -> form (value) -> mismatch. Only spaces and tabs are skipped before "a=" (a BOM there makes no candidate); U+2028 does not end a line. Guarantee: an accepted fp_viewer is the only fingerprint str0m can read from that SDP (str0m parses up to the first line it cannot parse and drops the rest, so a bare CR would split lines differently); an SDP str0m reads none from may pass, and DTLS then fails closed. Consumers assert both the verdict (expect) and `why` of every negative case: several cases are built so that a verifier missing one rule reaches a different verdict, and `why` names the rule that must refuse first.
